_comment: Hashes of the upstream artefacts every bridge document cites. Truncated to 16 hex, which is what the schema's pattern allows. Regenerate with tools/rehash.sh; a mismatch is rule R6 and it means an import is stale, not that the file is wrong.
_am_note: A sender's own plan changes between rounds -- that is the round working -- and this file holds one value per key. The unsuffixed plan key is the r1-era file (rev 9f971a8) that r1 and r2 both cite and must keep verifying; '@r<N>' is a second key for the revision a later round was distilled from (rev 35575cb). One key per round, added by the owning side, nothing overwritten. This is not a substitute for the `rev` field the README now requires on a ref: `rev` says which revision a ref means, the suffixed key is what lets R6 check two of them. Unsuffixed keys are at rev 9f971a8; '@r3' is 35575cb, '@r4' and '@r5' are aeea29d, all on branch worktree-work-2026-09-16 of the AM repo. The r2 import has two keys because r4 corrected it: the body is unedited and only `corrected_by` was added, so the r1-era hash still verifies for anything citing it from before.
_bd_note: bd: keys are added by the BD session. verify/ entries are at rev 07d1048 on branch microscope-link-survey, not on BD's main; every ref carries `rev`. The r2 key is UNSUFFIXED at the revision r4 and AM's r4 import cite, and '@r8' is the revision after 4652273 added gaps[].kind. Refreshing the unsuffixed key instead was tried and CASCADED: r4 then had to be refreshed, which broke r5 and r7, which cite r4. A sealed document's citation must not move because a later commit added metadata upstream -- that is what the suffixed-key convention is for.
